description_full: IRADIMED CORPORATION develops, manufactures, markets, and distributes magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) compatible intravenous infusion pump systems and MRI compatible patient vital signs monitoring systems and related accessories. The company offers MRidium 3870 and 3860+ MRI Compatible IV Infusion Pump System with associated disposable IV tubing sets; 3880 MRI compatible patient vital signs monitoring system; and 3600 FMD1 with remote alarm logging unit ferromagnetic detection device. It also provides non-magnetic IV poles, wireless remote displays/controls, side car pump modules, dose error reduction systems, and SpO2 monitoring with sensors and accessories. The company serves hospitals, acute care facilities, and outpatient imaging centers. It sells its products through direct field sales representatives, regional sales directors, clinical application specialists, and independent distributors in the United States and internationally. The company was incorporated in 1992 and is headquartered in Orlando, Florida.

financial_summary: iRadimed Corporation is a small-cap healthcare business with a $1.1B market cap on $84M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 85% against a 9% cost of capital — a 76-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 77% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $17M in free cash flow — roughly 21 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.11× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.4%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 35% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
